_comment: 🔮️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform: `ruststep` 0.4 registered as the real ISO 10303-21 reader for stdio.ifc 4/✳️any's exhaustive IfcMutation vocabulary, the mutation catalog it is measured against, and the tolerant structural comparison profile a re-serialized IFC4 exchange structure needs against an independently parsed one.

oracles.rationale:
🩹️ RECLASSIFIED (ticket SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION, shard A10, 2026-09-02). This entry was registered `third-party-library` on the strength of a real crate that does genuine codec work, but the mutation's expected RESULT is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs` -- its dispatch function's catch-all arm is `"mutation kind {...} has no oracle implementation"`, proof that every OTHER arm is an implementation, not a reading. Both halves of the comparison then descend from the same specification, so a shared misreading produces two agreeing wrong answers -- the one failure a differential oracle exists to catch. This is a `cross-semio-implementation`: a required SUPPLEMENT (metamorphic/inverse/round-trip evidence), never a substitute. A qualifying third-party reference for the mutation semantics is still owed. See $TICKET/📓️a10-oracle-honesty.md.

IFC4 rides the same ISO 10303-21 (STEP physical file / Part-21) exchange-structure grammar as AP214 -- ruststep's `ast::Exchange`/`ast::DataSection`/`ast::Record`/`ast::Parameter`/`ast::EntityInstance` all implement `FromStr` over the real Part-21 clear-text grammar at the SYNTAX level only; ruststep compiles no IFC4 EXPRESS schema module at all, so this is a genuinely schema-agnostic reader, confirmed against this subset's own real fixture (a real 2.5 MB IfcOpenShell 0.8.4 export of the Nakagin Capsule Tower, 24792 entities, parsed with zero errors -- see `../🦀️oracle.rs`'s own `parses_the_real_fixture_and_projects_it` test). It has NO writer at all: `ast::ser::to_record` only builds a `Record` from an already-typed Rust struct, and grepping the crate for `Display`/`fmt::Formatter` impls on `Exchange`/`DataSection`/`Record`/`Parameter` finds none -- there is no serialize path back to Part-21 text anywhere in the crate (the same finding this wave's STEP AP214 case already made independently). Per the fleet brief's §6, this rules out `@mode-differential`: ruststep cannot be a second PRODUCER of mutated bytes to diff against. It is registered here strictly as the INDEPENDENT READER role -- every real mutation this subset's own oracle dispatcher (`../🦀️oracle.rs`) performs (via ruststep's real parse plus this module's own from-scratch Part-21 writer, since none exists to reuse) is read back through a FRESH, independent `ruststep::ast::Exchange::from_str` call before being projected onto `semantic-ifc-v1`, and the identity round trip is checked the same way. This is real third-party evidence about the STRUCTURE of the result (entity graph shape, header schema, argument values as ruststep's own parser sees them), even though it cannot discharge a byte-level differential claim.

IfcOpenShell 0.8.4 is the reference open-source IFC implementation and, unlike `ruststep`, it both READS and WRITES ISO 10303-21: `ifcopenshell.open` runs its own C++ Part-21 parser against the real IFC4 EXPRESS schema and `ifcopenshell.file.to_string`/`write` re-serialize the whole exchange structure from the parsed model. That makes it a genuine second PRODUCER — the role `ruststep` cannot fill — and it is registered here for exactly the differential case `../../../../🧪️tests/differential-ifc-4` that claims it. It does NOT replace `ruststep-ifc-4-any-mutate`, which stays the schema-agnostic independent READER of `mutate-ifc-4`: IfcOpenShell is schema-BOUND, so it can neither produce nor faithfully read the four kinds of this subset's vocabulary that leave the IFC4 schema. Measured on this subset's own real fixture rather than assumed — retyping `#16976` to `RENAMED_PROXY` makes `ifcopenshell.file.from_string` return 16975 of 24792 entities with no error raised, a tenth positional argument on a nine-attribute entity is read back silently dropped, and `ifcopenshell.file.remove` documents and performs reference repair (`#16976` disappears from `#16991`'s member aggregate) where `IfcMutation::RemoveEntity` deliberately does not cascade. `set-entity-name`, `insert-entity-arg`, `remove-entity-arg` and `remove-entity` are therefore NOT claimed here and carry no differential scenario; the seven kinds that are claimed are produced end to end by IfcOpenShell and re-read from its own written bytes.

comparisonProfiles.description: IFC4 (ISO 10303-21 exchange structures carrying IFC4's own EXPRESS schema) compared by declared FILE_SCHEMA and the full id-keyed entity graph (name plus positional argument values, reals tolerant). Header timestamp, preprocessor/originating-system strings, comment placement and line-wrapping are writer freedom -- the same normative surface IfcDiff/IfcMutation themselves operate over.
